entries.title: Bleeding Control Basics
entries.summary: Static reference for severe bleeding response before transport or EMS handoff.

sections.title: Immediate Actions
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Put firm direct pressure on the wound.
- Use clean absorbent material if available.
- Add more material without repeatedly lifting the first layer.
sections.plainText: Put firm direct pressure on the wound. Use clean absorbent material if available. Add more material without repeatedly lifting the first layer.

sections.title: Escalate Pressure
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- If direct pressure fails and the wound is on a limb, use a commercial tourniquet only if you already have one and understand its instructions.
- Note the time and keep the person still and warm.
sections.plainText: If direct pressure fails and the wound is on a limb, use a commercial tourniquet only if you already have one and understand its instructions. Note the time and keep the person still and warm.

sections.title: Get Help Now
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Seek urgent care for spurting blood, soaking through dressings, amputation, or signs of shock.
- Do not remove deeply embedded objects unless current local guidance says to do so.
sections.plainText: Seek urgent care for spurting blood, soaking through dressings, amputation, or signs of shock. Do not remove deeply embedded objects unless current local guidance says to do so.

mediaAttachments.caption: A pressure pad and wrap can help keep direct pressure in place while you keep checking below the dressing.
mediaAttachments.accessibilityLabel: Illustration showing a pressure dressing wrapped over a bleeding arm injury.

mediaAttachments.caption: Short local clip showing the dressing pad, wrap path, and final circulation check direction.
mediaAttachments.accessibilityLabel: Offline video showing a pressure dressing sequence on a forearm.
mediaAttachments.transcript: Place the pad over the wound. Wrap firmly enough to hold pressure. Check below the dressing for warmth, color, and feeling. Add more material on top if bleeding continues and seek urgent care if bleeding does not stop.

questions.prompt: If bleeding keeps showing through the dressing, what does this static reference tell you to do first?

options.text: Add more absorbent material without repeatedly lifting the first layer.
Remove the first layer over and over to inspect the wound.

questions.explanation: The reference keeps the response conservative: maintain direct pressure and add material on top rather than disrupting the first layer.

questions.prompt: Which situation is an escalation cue for urgent care?

options.text: Spurting blood, soaking through dressings, or signs of shock.

questions.explanation: The field reference calls out spurting blood, soaked dressings, amputation, and shock as urgent escalation cues.

entries.title: Minor Burn Cooling Reference
entries.summary: Static reference for brief cooling, covering, and escalation decisions after a minor burn.

sections.title: Cool
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Cool the area with clean running water when available.
- Remove rings or tight items before swelling starts.
sections.plainText: Cool the area with clean running water when available. Remove rings or tight items before swelling starts.

sections.title: Cover
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Cover loosely with a clean, non-stick dressing.
- Keep the area clean and stop if pain sharply worsens.
sections.plainText: Cover loosely with a clean, non-stick dressing. Keep the area clean and stop if pain sharply worsens.

sections.title: Escalate
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Seek urgent care for burns to the face, hands, genitals, large areas, or any burn linked to smoke inhalation.
- Do not use ice, butter, or ointments you would not already trust on broken skin.
sections.plainText: Seek urgent care for burns to the face, hands, genitals, large areas, or any burn linked to smoke inhalation. Do not use ice, butter, or ointments you would not already trust on broken skin.

entries.title: Recovery Position Reminder
entries.summary: Static reminder for rolling an unresponsive breathing person onto their side when spinal injury is not suspected.

sections.title: Before Rolling
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Confirm the person is breathing.
- Check the scene and stop if a spinal injury is strongly suspected or the person cannot be moved safely.
sections.plainText: Confirm the person is breathing. Check the scene and stop if a spinal injury is strongly suspected or the person cannot be moved safely.

sections.title: Roll To The Side
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Move the far arm across the chest.
- Bend the top knee and roll the person toward you onto their side.
- Tilt the head slightly back to help keep the airway open.
sections.plainText: Move the far arm across the chest. Bend the top knee and roll the person toward you onto their side. Tilt the head slightly back to help keep the airway open.

sections.title: Keep Watching
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Keep checking breathing and responsiveness.
- If vomiting starts or breathing changes, re-check position and seek urgent help.
sections.plainText: Keep checking breathing and responsiveness. If vomiting starts or breathing changes, re-check position and seek urgent help.

mediaAttachments.caption: Roll to the side, bend the top knee, and keep the head slightly tilted back while you keep checking breathing.
mediaAttachments.accessibilityLabel: Illustration showing the recovery position with the head tilted back and the top knee bent.

entries.title: Basic Splint Stabilization Reference
entries.summary: Static reminder for padding, supporting, and securing an injured limb before transport.

sections.title: Support First
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Support the injured limb in the position found.
- Stop if movement sharply increases pain or meets strong resistance.
sections.plainText: Support the injured limb in the position found. Stop if movement sharply increases pain or meets strong resistance.

sections.title: Pad And Secure
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Place padding between the limb and the splint.
- Secure above and below the injury site instead of cinching directly over it.
sections.plainText: Place padding between the limb and the splint. Secure above and below the injury site instead of cinching directly over it.

sections.title: Re-Check
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Re-check warmth, color, and feeling below the splint after securing it.
- Seek urgent care for deformity, numbness, or circulation changes.
sections.plainText: Re-check warmth, color, and feeling below the splint after securing it. Seek urgent care for deformity, numbness, or circulation changes.

mediaAttachments.caption: Pad the splint, secure it above and below the injury, and re-check circulation below the wrap points.
mediaAttachments.accessibilityLabel: Illustration showing a padded splint secured above and below a forearm injury.

entries.title: Square Knot Reference
entries.summary: Starter reference for joining two rope ends of similar size when the load is stable and non-life-safety.

sections.title: Use Case
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Join similar rope ends for bundling, lashing, or simple staging tasks.
- Keep the load stable and easy to inspect.
sections.plainText: Join similar rope ends for bundling, lashing, or simple staging tasks. Keep the load stable and easy to inspect.

sections.title: Tie Sequence
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Left over right and tuck.
- Then right over left and tuck.
- Dress the knot so both ends lie flat and even.
sections.plainText: Left over right and tuck. Then right over left and tuck. Dress the knot so both ends lie flat and even.

sections.title: Do Not Use
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Do not use for life safety, climbing, or critical towing loads.
- Re-tie if the finished knot capsizes or one side looks twisted.
sections.plainText: Do not use for life safety, climbing, or critical towing loads. Re-tie if the finished knot capsizes or one side looks twisted.

mediaAttachments.caption: Tie left over right, then right over left, and dress the knot flat before you trust it for bundling.
mediaAttachments.accessibilityLabel: Illustration showing the two crossing steps used to finish a square knot.

entries.title: Bowline Reference
entries.summary: Starter reference for making a fixed loop that stays easy to untie after light household or staging loads.

sections.title: Use Case
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Make a fixed loop at the end of a rope for tying around an object or clipping into a non-life-safety staging point.
- Keep the load static and inspectable.
sections.plainText: Make a fixed loop at the end of a rope for tying around an object or clipping into a non-life-safety staging point. Keep the load static and inspectable.

sections.title: Tie Sequence
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Make a small loop in the standing part.
- Bring the tail up through the loop, around the standing part, and back down through the same loop.
- Dress the loop and tighten the knot before loading it.
sections.plainText: Make a small loop in the standing part. Bring the tail up through the loop, around the standing part, and back down through the same loop. Dress the loop and tighten the knot before loading it.

sections.title: Do Not Use
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Do not treat this as climbing or rescue instruction.
- Re-tie if the loop size changes unexpectedly or the knot was tied in the wrong direction.
sections.plainText: Do not treat this as climbing or rescue instruction. Re-tie if the loop size changes unexpectedly or the knot was tied in the wrong direction.

mediaAttachments.caption: Make the small loop first, then bring the tail up through it, around the standing part, and back down.
mediaAttachments.accessibilityLabel: Illustration showing the three-step bowline path and the finished fixed loop.

questions.prompt: What kind of loop is the bowline meant to create in this starter reference?

options.text: A fixed loop that stays the same size when dressed correctly.
A slip loop that keeps tightening under pull.

questions.explanation: This reference treats the bowline as a fixed loop for light, inspectable household or staging loads.

questions.prompt: Which path matches the bowline sequence in this app?

options.text: Up through the loop, around the standing part, and back down through the same loop.
Wrap both ends together until the loop disappears.
Cross the tails twice and stop there.

questions.explanation: The mnemonic path matters because it keeps the loop fixed and easier to inspect before light use.

entries.title: Clove Hitch Reference
entries.summary: Starter reference for staging a rope quickly around a post when the load can be watched and adjusted.

sections.title: Use Case
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Stage a rope quickly around a post or rail.
- Best for temporary lashing or controlled tension that you can keep checking.
sections.plainText: Stage a rope quickly around a post or rail. Best for temporary lashing or controlled tension that you can keep checking.

sections.title: Tie Sequence
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Wrap around the post once.
- Cross over the standing part and wrap again.
- Tuck the working end under the crossing turn and dress the wraps flat.
sections.plainText: Wrap around the post once. Cross over the standing part and wrap again. Tuck the working end under the crossing turn and dress the wraps flat.

sections.title: Do Not Use
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Back it up if vibration, shaking, or repeated movement is likely.
- Do not treat this as a life-safety anchor.
sections.plainText: Back it up if vibration, shaking, or repeated movement is likely. Do not treat this as a life-safety anchor.

mediaAttachments.caption: Make two wraps around the post, cross them on the front, and dress them flat before loading.
mediaAttachments.accessibilityLabel: Illustration showing the two wraps and front crossing of a clove hitch around a post.

entries.title: Trucker's Hitch Reference
entries.summary: Starter reference for creating mechanical advantage when tensioning a load that you can re-check often.

sections.title: Use Case
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Tension a tarp line or strap a household load that you can re-check.
- Keep the system simple and inspectable.
sections.plainText: Tension a tarp line or strap a household load that you can re-check. Keep the system simple and inspectable.

sections.title: Tie Sequence
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Anchor one end.
- Form a small loop in the standing part.
- Run the working end through the loop and pull to tension before securing the finish.
sections.plainText: Anchor one end. Form a small loop in the standing part. Run the working end through the loop and pull to tension before securing the finish.

sections.title: Do Not Use
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Do not treat it as a rescue hauling system.
- Re-check the load after movement or road vibration.
sections.plainText: Do not treat it as a rescue hauling system. Re-check the load after movement or road vibration.

mediaAttachments.caption: Anchor one end, make a mid-line loop, and pull through it to tension a load you can keep inspecting.
mediaAttachments.accessibilityLabel: Illustration showing an anchor point, a mid-line loop, and the hauling direction for a trucker's hitch.

entries.title: Heat Stress Response Reference
entries.summary: Reviewed static cues for cooling early and escalating when heat stress stops improving.

sections.title: Move And Cool
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Move into shade or the coolest available room.
- Loosen excess clothing and cool with damp cloths or airflow if tolerated.
sections.plainText: Move into shade or the coolest available room. Loosen excess clothing and cool with damp cloths or airflow if tolerated.

sections.title: Support
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Offer water only if the person is awake, alert, and able to swallow.
- Reduce exertion immediately even if symptoms seem mild.
sections.plainText: Offer water only if the person is awake, alert, and able to swallow. Reduce exertion immediately even if symptoms seem mild.

sections.title: Escalate Now
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Seek urgent care for confusion, fainting, repeated vomiting, or no improvement after cooling begins.
- Do not keep exercising or use alcohol as a cooling shortcut.
sections.plainText: Seek urgent care for confusion, fainting, repeated vomiting, or no improvement after cooling begins. Do not keep exercising or use alcohol as a cooling shortcut.

entries.title: Cold Exposure Rewarming Reference
entries.summary: Static rewarming notes for wet, cold, and low-heat conditions before transport.

sections.title: Dry First
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Move out of wind and wet clothing quickly.
- Replace with dry layers, head covering, and insulation from the ground.
sections.plainText: Move out of wind and wet clothing quickly. Replace with dry layers, head covering, and insulation from the ground.

sections.title: Warm Gradually
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Use shared body heat, blankets, and warm non-alcoholic drinks if the person is awake and able to swallow.
- Handle the person gently if they are severely cold or exhausted.
sections.plainText: Use shared body heat, blankets, and warm non-alcoholic drinks if the person is awake and able to swallow. Handle the person gently if they are severely cold or exhausted.

sections.title: Escalate Now
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Seek urgent care for confusion, slurred speech, unusual clumsiness, or shivering that stops.
- Do not place numb skin against direct intense heat.
sections.plainText: Seek urgent care for confusion, slurred speech, unusual clumsiness, or shivering that stops. Do not place numb skin against direct intense heat.

entries.title: Household Water Disinfection Reference
entries.summary: Concise reference for clarifying, treating, storing, and separating questionable water.

sections.title: Clarify First
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Let particles settle or strain water through a clean cloth before chemical treatment.
- Keep untreated and treated containers clearly separate.
sections.plainText: Let particles settle or strain water through a clean cloth before chemical treatment. Keep untreated and treated containers clearly separate.

sections.title: Use Known Methods
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Use only products and instructions you already store with the kit.
- Boil when you have a safe fuel and ventilation plan and the water source is uncertain.
sections.plainText: Use only products and instructions you already store with the kit. Boil when you have a safe fuel and ventilation plan and the water source is uncertain.

sections.title: Avoid Improvisation
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Do not mix chemicals or improvise doses.
- Re-treat or discard water if the container, timing, or product is uncertain.
sections.plainText: Do not mix chemicals or improvise doses. Re-treat or discard water if the container, timing, or product is uncertain.

entries.title: Visual And Radio Signal Reference
entries.summary: Simple offline signaling cues for panels, lights, whistles, and short radio traffic.

sections.title: Make It Obvious
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Use high-contrast panels, repeated flashes, or simple whistle patterns that can be repeated.
- Keep the signal visible from likely approach routes.
sections.plainText: Use high-contrast panels, repeated flashes, or simple whistle patterns that can be repeated. Keep the signal visible from likely approach routes.

sections.title: Keep Messages Short
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Lead with location, immediate need, and number of people.
- Repeat the same wording instead of improvising a new description each time.
sections.plainText: Lead with location, immediate need, and number of people. Repeat the same wording instead of improvising a new description each time.

sections.title: Conserve Power
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Use scheduled check-in windows for battery-powered signaling.
- Protect backup batteries, light sources, and radios from rain and impact.
sections.plainText: Use scheduled check-in windows for battery-powered signaling. Protect backup batteries, light sources, and radios from rain and impact.

entries.title: Unscented Bleach Vs Splashless Bleach
entries.summary: Comparison notes for bleach products that look similar but should not be treated as interchangeable for water work.

sections.title: Use Only Plain Products
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Plain, unscented household bleach may appear in older emergency references.
- Splashless, scented, or added-cleaner products should not be assumed equivalent.
sections.plainText: Plain, unscented household bleach may appear in older emergency references. Splashless, scented, or added-cleaner products should not be assumed equivalent.

sections.title: Check The Label
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Look for fragrance, thickener, color-safe, or cleaner language before you store it with water treatment gear.
- Keep the original container and expiration information with the product.
sections.plainText: Look for fragrance, thickener, color-safe, or cleaner language before you store it with water treatment gear. Keep the original container and expiration information with the product.

sections.title: Do Not Guess
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- If the product type is unclear, do not use it for water treatment.
- Default to boiling or another method you already understand instead of improvising chemistry.
sections.plainText: If the product type is unclear, do not use it for water treatment. Default to boiling or another method you already understand instead of improvising chemistry.

entries.title: NIOSH Respirator Vs Loose Dust Mask
entries.summary: Conservative comparison notes for smoke and ash protection gear that is easy to confuse at a glance.

sections.title: What You Are Looking For
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- A smoke-ready respirator reference should name the standard it meets and fit closely to the face.
- A loose dust mask or simple face covering may reduce nuisance dust but should not be assumed equivalent.
sections.plainText: A smoke-ready respirator reference should name the standard it meets and fit closely to the face. A loose dust mask or simple face covering may reduce nuisance dust but should not be assumed equivalent.

sections.title: Check Before You Need It
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- Store labeled respirators with the clean-room kit, not mixed loose with other masks.
- Practice fit checks before smoke season rather than during an evacuation rush.
sections.plainText: Store labeled respirators with the clean-room kit, not mixed loose with other masks. Practice fit checks before smoke season rather than during an evacuation rush.

sections.title: Use Caution
sections.bodyMarkdown:
- If the mask will not seal, is wet, or causes distress, move to cleaner air sooner instead of forcing it.
- Do not promise yourself respirator protection from gear you have not already identified and staged.
sections.plainText: If the mask will not seal, is wet, or causes distress, move to cleaner air sooner instead of forcing it. Do not promise yourself respirator protection from gear you have not already identified and staged.
